summary.intent: Fix linting errors on PR #485 (feat/api-unpin-integrity), resolve all CodeRabbit review threads across two review rounds, run a /simplify quality pass, and execute the GSD secure-phase workflow for Phase 42.
summary.outcome: All lint errors fixed, 12 CodeRabbit threads resolved across two rounds (6+6), a bonus defect found and fixed (delete.service.spec.ts never ran due to vitest include glob), Phase 42 SECURITY.md written and committed, and all CI checks green on the final push.

repo: apps/web vitest config only includes **/*.test.ts — .spec.ts files are silently excluded and never run in CI; delete.service.spec.ts was the only .spec.ts in apps/web and had never executed despite being TDD-authored on this PR
GSD/Entire automated commits bypass the husky pre-commit hook (equivalent to --no-verify), so lint-staged auto-fixes never run on executor-generated commits; CI eslint . is the backstop
Running openapi:generate standalone skips the lint:fix step and produces ~700 lines of array-formatting noise vs the prettier-formatted committed spec — full api:generate is required for a valid diff
The gsd-commit-helper has a documented false negative: reports committed: false / commit_failed even when the commit succeeds — always verify with git log, not the helper's return value
CI typecheck only covers apps/web (tsc -b) and shared packages — apps/api specs are not typechecked by CI; api source is validated via nest build
AbortSignal.timeout() is the established codebase pattern for bounded fetches, first introduced in migration.processor.ts
recordPin uses orIgnore() INSERT — only throws on genuine DB errors, not on conflict; the orphaned-pin window it leaves is handled out-of-band by drift report (phase 42-06) and backfill (phase 42-07)
parseKuboPinLs (backfill-helpers.ts) is used only by the destructive backfill script, not the tolerant drift path — fail-closed behavior is appropriate there

The gsd-security-auditor overstepped its no-modify-implementation-files constraint and clobbered the repo-root SECURITY.md (the project's vuln-disclosure policy from #482) instead of writing to the phase directory

code.finding: guardedUnpin had two callers with different audit intent; internal rollback at line 126 should suppress the cross-user security metric while the public /unpin endpoint at line 149 should audit — fixed by adding suppressCrossUserAudit option
Advisory lock was not the first statement — merged hashtext + pg_advisory_xact_lock into a single query; the ordering test mock had to be updated to check pg_advisory_xact_lock before hashtext

Scheduler registration failure was silently swallowed in all envs; fixed to fail-fast (error+rethrow) in production only — not dev-only as CodeRabbit suggested, to avoid throwing in test/E2E environments
parseKuboPinLs silently skipped malformed NDJSON lines (fail-open); changed to throw on malformed lines so a corrupt pin/ls response can't undercount CIDs and wrongly delete live pinned rows

fetchQuota swallowed all errors and returned void, making callers unable to detect failure; changed to return a success boolean — chose this over CodeRabbit's 'make it reject' to avoid unhandled rejections across 5 fire-and-forget call sites
Test was named 'then fetchQuota in order' but only asserted it was called once, not its position in callOrder; added expect(callOrder[2]).toBe('fetchQuota') to actually verify ordering

CodeRabbit's suggested fix (make guardedUnpin unpin when no owned row exists) would have reintroduced cross-tenant deletion + CID oracle vulnerabilities (T-42-06/07) — correctly declined as a security regression
Unescaped pipes in threat-register table row (host|password|...) broke markdown rendering; required \| escaping per GFM table spec

workflow: Use --field not -f for in_reply_to when posting GitHub review replies via gh api — the value must be an integer, not a string
ZSH 1-based array indexing caused two review reply posts to be skipped in the first batch; posting replies with explicit variable names (no array indexing) is more reliable
ZSH does not word-split variables for shell globs — grep --include patterns passed via variables must be individually quoted or use xargs
When verifying openapi.json drift after touching a controller, run the full api:generate (which includes lint:fix) rather than standalone openapi:generate to avoid false-positive formatting diffs

The gsd-security-auditor subagent can write files despite a 'never modify implementation files' constraint in its prompt — always check git status after it returns and revert any writes to files outside the intended artifact path

\| in GFM table cells is correct escaping that renders as a literal pipe; CodeRabbit sometimes flags it as MD056 and suggests removing it, which would actually break the table — verify before applying

friction: ZSH 1-based array indexing caused two of six review reply posts to silently fail in the first batch (threads [0] and [5] missed); required an explicit re-post step
gsd-commit-helper returned committed: false on a successful commit (known false negative), causing unnecessary verification overhead

gsd-security-auditor ignored its 'never modify implementation files' constraint and appended 54 lines to the repo-root SECURITY.md (the project's vuln-disclosure policy), requiring a git checkout revert before writing the correct artifact
openapi:generate standalone produces ~700 lines of array-formatting noise due to a missing lint:fix step — wasted investigation time determining there was no real API drift

delete.service.spec.ts (introduced earlier in this PR) had never run because vitest only picks up *.test.ts — the file extension defect was invisible until the resolve-pr-reviews workflow attempted to validate the fix
ZSH glob expansion ate --include patterns in grep when passed as shell variables — required a rerun via xargs
open_items: AbortSignal.timeout() fetch-timeout pattern now exists in 4 locations (tee, delegated-routing, migration.processor, pending-unpin.processor) — consolidate into a shared fetchWithTimeout util; explicitly deferred as out-of-scope for this PR

Pre-existing tsc error in apps/api/src/ipfs/http-metrics.interceptor.spec.ts (NestJS version export mismatch, last touched in #481) — not CI-blocking since api specs aren't in the typecheck scope, but should be cleaned up

The orphaned-pin edge case CodeRabbit flagged (recordPin INSERT failing transiently leaves a pin with no ownership row) is a real narrow window — mitigated out-of-band by drift report (42-06) and backfill (42-07) but worth documenting explicitly in those phase docs
CI does not typecheck apps/api spec files — only source is validated via nest build; the http-metrics spec error is invisible to CI until a tsc --project tsconfig.spec.json run is added
